Tailcat listener

Source: R/listener.R
TailcatListener.Rd

A listener accepts TCP connections or UDP flows on one port of a TailcatServer. Listeners are created by TailcatServer$listen(), not directly.

Accepted connections belong to the server rather than the listener: closing the listener stops new connections but leaves accepted ones open, while closing the server closes everything.

Once the listener or its server is closed, every method other than $close(), $stop_serving(), $format(), and $print(), and every field other than $is_closed and $server, raises a tailcat_closed error. Timeouts (including timeout = 0, a poll) and errors are described in TailcatServer.

Serving connections

$serve(handler) starts an accept loop driven by the later event loop and returns immediately. Each new connection is passed to handler(conn) on the main R thread. The loop only makes progress while the event loop runs: when R is idle at the console, inside Shiny or httpuv, or while a script calls later::run_now() in a loop. Blocking calls inside the handler (such as conn$read()) hold up the loop until they return, so long-running handlers should use the _async() methods and return the resulting promise. A handler may return a promise (or anything promises::is.promising() accepts): if it rejects, the rejection is treated like an error signaled by the handler, so on_error is called and the connection is closed. The loop does not wait for the promise before accepting the next connection. The loop ends quietly when the listener or the server is closed, or when $stop_serving() is called; $stop_serving() leaves the listener open, so it can accept connections again or serve with a new handler.

Active bindings

port

The port number being listened on.

local_address

The local endpoint as "host:port" on the server's tailcat network (not the secret tailcat address).

network

"tcp" or "udp".

server

The owning TailcatServer.

is_closed

TRUE once the listener or its server has been closed.

TailcatListener$new()

Internal constructor; use TailcatServer$listen().

Usage

TailcatListener$new(handle, server, network)

Arguments

handle

Native listener handle.

server

The owning TailcatServer.

network

Integer network code.

TailcatListener$accept()

Wait for the next connection (TCP) or new flow (UDP). A timeout ends only this call; the listener stays usable.

Usage

TailcatListener$accept(timeout = Inf)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls (returns a connection that is already waiting).

Returns

A TailcatConnection.

TailcatListener$accept_async()

Asynchronous version of $accept().

Usage

TailcatListener$accept_async(timeout = Inf)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

A promise resolving with a TailcatConnection.

TailcatListener$serve()

Start an asynchronous accept loop that calls handler(conn) for every connection. See the section on serving connections.

Usage

TailcatListener$serve(handler, on_error = NULL)

Arguments

handler

A function of one argument, the TailcatConnection. It may return a promise.

on_error

A function function(cond, conn) called when handler signals an error or the promise it returned rejects (or when accepting fails, with conn = NULL), or NULL to turn such errors into warnings (signaled from the later event loop). After a handler error the connection is closed. An error signaled by on_error itself is turned into a warning.

Returns

The listener, invisibly. Calling it on a listener that is already serving raises a tailcat_failure error (call $stop_serving() first), and on a closed listener a tailcat_closed error.

TailcatListener$stop_serving()

Stop the accept loop started by $serve() without closing the listener. The pending accept is canceled; connections already accepted are not affected, and a connection whose accept completed at the same moment is still passed to the handler. Calling it when the listener is not serving does nothing.

Usage

TailcatListener$stop_serving()

Returns

The listener, invisibly.

TailcatListener$close()

Stop accepting connections. Accepted connections stay open. Closing twice is harmless.

Usage

TailcatListener$close()

Returns

The listener, invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
srv = TailcatServer$new()
lst = srv$listen(7)
lst$serve(function(conn) {
  promises::then(conn$read_all_async(timeout = 30), function(data) {
    conn$write(data)
    conn$close()
  })
})
srv$address
} # }
